AAPL

LLY
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Apple (AAPL) shares look expensive heading into 2027, despite the company's strong growth prospects. Shares of the iPhone maker have soared in 2026, easily outperforming the Nasdaq-100 (NDX) as tracked by the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ). This comes as Apple has delivered higher sales and revenues this year, a trend analysts expect to continue into Fiscal 2027.

What is more, Apple may benefit from higher device sales should memory costs normalize, potentially making the shares interesting for investors looking to diversify their artificial intelligence (AI) exposure away from current high memory cost beneficiaries such as Micron (MU).

Despite these positives for the Apple investment case, my rating on the shares remains a Hold. I believe that with the stock trading at 37.08x analysts' consensus 2027 earnings per share (EPS) estimate of $9.40, the outlook for investor returns is quite modest even as the company is likely to continue its strong underlying performance.

Apple's Record Net Income and EPS

Apple delivered Q4 2026 EPS of $2.10, a 14% increase relative to the prior-year quarter and a Q4 record for the company from a historical perspective. While results were boosted by a $0.05 per share one-off tariff refund, underlying performance was nevertheless quite strong.

Case in point, Apple sales increased 12% year-over-year, driven by the low-margin products segment. Apple cited strong iPhone demand as a key revenue driver. Growth in the high-margin services business was somewhat weaker, at 10% year-over-year. A 32% year-over-year increase in research & development expenses was a relative disappointment, although this should help Apple's innovation over the medium term.

CEO John Ternus was quite optimistic for the company's prospects going into Q1 2027. He said, "We're closing the year with our most ambitious lineup yet. That includes the iPhone Duo, the most transformational iPhone since the original, alongside iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, our most powerful iPhones yet. We also just introduced a whole new generation of hardware for the home and brought Touch to Mac for the first time. Together with the all-new Siri AI, it's an incredible lineup to carry us into the holiday season."

detail:

OKXICE Gets Ready for 24/7 Markets - Moby
BREAKING NEWS

Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.

Get your sugar-free Red Bull and multiple-monitor setup ready, because beginning November 23, eligible U.S. customers will be able to trade digital securities 24/7 through the OKXICE Tokenized Securities Venue, or TSV.

More than 70 assets are expected to list on the venue, OKXICE said. They include securities from Better.com, BitGo, Circle, Coinbase, Robinhood, Securitize and Strategy, plus 59 Direxion ETFs meant to give users "diversified exposure across assets, markets and styles." Which 59 funds made the cut hasn't been made public, but either way, users won't own the fund's basket. Each token represents a share of the ETF itself. If you're confused, don't feel bad. It's confusing. Direxion is mostly a leveraged and inverse ETF shop, so its flagship index and sector funds are probably in.

That's where it gets… interesting and a little contentious. All of the MAG 7 (Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, Tesla and Meta) objected to tokens of their stock trading on the venue, as have JPMorgan Chase, Goldman Sachs and dozens of others. But an objection only covers a company's own stock. The issuer of an ETF token is Direxion, so the funds can list anyway, even though many of them are built on the big names that opted out.

Apple can say no to Apple tokens, but it can't say no to a fund built around Apple. As noted, confusing.

To throw yet another curveball into this foray into 24/7 trading and agentic trading, former New York Governor Andrew M. Cuomo is tied up with all of this.

One stock. Nvidia-level potential. 30M+ investors trust Moby to find it first. Get the pick. Tap here.

"The SEC has created a real opening for American markets to lead the next era of finance," Cuomo, co-chair of OKXICE, said. "OKXICE TSV gives first movers the opportunity to bring their securities on-chain through a compliant venue built for 24/7 markets and real shareholder rights. The future of finance is on-chain, and we have an opportunity to build it here in America, with the standards, safeguards and ambition that investors expect."

Quite the pivot, given Cuomo is the subject of a DOJ criminal investigation connected to the coronavirus pandemic. That said, it was led by Jeanine Pirro, who has since been let go by the Trump administration. We wish them both well.

Trading on TSV will happen via automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pools built on Uniswap v4 on X Layer, OKX's Ethereum Layer 2 network, per OKX's presser. Securitize is behind the actual tokenization of the assets, each backed one-to-one by an underlying U.S. share. All digital assets will be held securely via users' digital wallets after the typical KYC, geographic location and "other eligibility requirements."

It should be an interesting launch, truly putting to the test the hype of crypto tokenization, agentic trading and AI.

Will Nokia (NYSE:NOK) close at or above $9.39, the October 29 rebound high identified by TradingKey's Alan Long, by December 31, 2026? The American depositary receipts (ADRs) traded at $8.41 Wednesday morning, up 2% on the session. Long noted the shares plunged 9.7% on November 5 to a recent low of $7.36, and they then rose for three straight sessions.

24/7 Wall St.
Price Levels That Settle the Call

Long's November 11 TradingKey chart analysis places key resistance near $8.40. Resistance is a price where sellers have repeatedly stopped rallies. In Long's reading, a clean break above it opens a run toward $9.39, with the next resistance at $9.65. Support is the opposite: a floor where buyers have stepped in before. Long puts that zone between $7.90 and $8.00. Moving averages, which track a stock's average closing price over a set number of days, help traders judge trend direction. A price holding above them signals that buyers have control.

NOK Price Scenario — 24/7 Wall St.
Three Reasons the Rebound Extends
1. Compounding AI Demand

Nokia reported that third-quarter AI and cloud revenue rose 123% year over year. Nokia also said order intake in the segment climbed 118% to €1.5 billion. Management said demand exceeds supply in both Optical and IP Networks, and it guided Q4 net sales to rise 20% to 24% sequentially. It also expects full-year comparable operating profit above the midpoint of its €2.1 billion to €2.6 billion outlook.

43 ETFs grew their AMD positions on Nov. 9, while 22 ETFs cut their holdings, according to data from GuruFocus.

The iShares Semiconductor ETF was the biggest gainer, gaining 776,056 AMD shares worth around $394.7 million.

The purchase boosted the fund's holdings 10.55% to 8.13 million shares or 10.01% of its portfolio.

Invesco QQQ bought an additional 182,016 shares valued at $92.6 million while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF purchased 108,445 shares valued at $55.2 million.

Buying came as chipmakers have seen fresh interest in the wake of recent market dips.

AMD had trailing 12-month sales of $45.44 billion, up 40% from a year earlier, according to GuruFocus. The company had a gross margin of 51.2% and a net margin of 16.7%.

That said, value is still an issue. AMD sold at about 112 times profits and at a GF Value estimate of $316.19, a significant discount to the market price of $515.21. The firm has a GF Score of 82 out of 100.

The numbers imply a robust appetite for ETFs, but increases in fund ownership do not equate to necessary direct financial investment into AMD.

Investors will want to see if ETF purchasing continues and if future earnings growth will justify the stock's value.
